s1.syndrome_frame: Malocclusion with unerupted tooth and associated radiopaque lesion
salient_findings: Radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
key_facts: 22-year-old woman
All permanent teeth erupted except third molars and lower left lateral incisor
Mild spacing between lower left central incisor and canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion
Crowding in maxillary anterior region
No history of prior dental extractions
Panoramic radiograph and mandibular occlusal film showed unerupted tooth and radiopaque lesion
Radiopaque lesion surrounded by thin radiolucent halo

shortlist.label: Compound odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common mixed odontogenic tumor characterized by multiple tooth-like structures, consistent with radiopaque lesion and unerupted tooth

shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Type of odontogenic tumor that can cause tooth impaction and is associated with a radiopaque lesion

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Common odontogenic tumor that can surround and prevent eruption of a tooth, consistent with radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Type of odontogenic cyst that can surround and prevent eruption of a tooth, although less likely given the radiopaque nature of the lesion

shortlist.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Rare odontogenic tumor that can present with a radiopaque lesion and is associated with unerupted teeth

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined radiopaque lesion surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, associated with an unerupted tooth, is consistent with the characteristics of a compound odontoma, which is a type of odontogenic tumor that can obstruct tooth eruption.

rejected.label: Complex odontoma
rejected.why: Complex odontomas typically present as a single, large radiopaque mass, whereas the described lesion is associated with an unerupted tooth and has a distinct appearance.

rejected.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumors often have a less radiopaque appearance and are not typically surrounded by a radiolucent halo.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: Dentigerous cysts are characterized by a radiolucent lesion surrounding the crown of an unerupted tooth, which does not match the radiopaque lesion described.

rejected.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumors can have a mixed radiolucent and radiopaque appearance, but the described lesion's characteristics are more consistent with a compound odontoma.
